negative_reviews.author: Julia x
negative_reviews.text:
Came here for the £5 ramen deal, we scanned the qr codes to make it £5 i don’t know if the waitress didn’t scan it properly but the total came out to be £27.50. It should’ve been £9 with the sides plus drink.

Extremely disappointed did not come here to pay nearly £30 the ramen wasn’t that good, steak was awful. Also ordered a diet coke and they said they said they’re out of gas so we could not get any kind of fizzy drinks.

negative_reviews.author: Isha Shah
negative_reviews.text:
Vegans be ware! They served me real eggs.
Maybe it was a bad day in the restaurant was busy so I’d like to give people grace. But me and my friend both ordered Vegan Ramen from the Vegan menu and even asked the waiter what was the best vegan Ramen there was? When our balls came, they both had egg in it. My friend wasn’t Vegan so I asked her to try the egg and bacon. She said the egg tasted a real egg and the bacon didn’t. I then asked the waiter if the egg was real and he said yes, I looked at him shocked I asked him for a vegan Ramen instead of apologising he asked me are you sure? As if I didn’t mention Vegan Ramen enough? As a Vegan there’s stereotype we always talk about us being Vegan and yes, that was me so I’m pretty sure I mentioned me being Vegan at least five times in the ordering interaction. There was no accountability or apology which is absolutely crazy. We asked for tapwater and that never came so I had to ask for that two times before it did. I get restaurants are busy and packed but Lets Be real this mistake is absolutely insane. So Vegan, if you’re gonna eat it be absolutely aware that you could be getting served real animal products which is a scary thought.

issues: Covers up again on more £5 and free ramen redemptions, sales on target; labour 0.5% over target because of the promotion.

Deliveroo: a few amber metrics; the manager on the pass now reminds the kitchen when a delivery order comes through, all Deliveroo orders are photographed into a new WhatsApp group chat, the person on the pass hands orders to riders when the bar is busy, and Deliveroo notes are going back into each bag to lift ratings.
Food cost: the site started topping up stock last week after speaking with Michael.

Reviews: three last week; a 3 star with no comment, one where the £5 discount was not applied at settlement (replied on Google, balance to be refunded when the customer gets in touch), and a 2 star claiming egg on a vegan tantan, which the site could not find in that week's orders and thinks may not be from this site (replied to investigate).
Recruiting one sushi chef and one full time kitchen assistant.
Inka approved one seasonal FOH hire for three months to cover Christmas; Hana will open the job post and the role ends in January.
Map was down on Monday, which affected things slightly.

Region: a new company wide performance dashboard (trialled at M14) will give week on week, month on month and quarter on quarter comparisons; GMs must resolve their outstanding tasks and post updates on it within a week, and Inka will send the link once Michael's guide video is ready.
Region: staff should proactively offer free frozen ramen to students (ask if they are a student, have their ID and have signed up to the app) to lift frozen ramen exposure and Slerp sign ups.
Region: remaining scratch pot vouchers (500 printed) can still be given out until 22/10, crossing out the 23/10 expiry date with a Sharpie.
Region: all bubble tea cups, lids and straws must be ordered only from Boba Box using the product codes shared on Kobas, with flat lids replacing dome lids at marketing's request.

Region: an extra labour margin of up to 2% is allowed for high redemption sites while £5, £3 and 50% off ramen volumes stay high (Nottingham 23%, Leeds 22%), on condition that service and food quality stay high.
Region: food cost may temporarily run toward 30% for two to three weeks while chefs top up to a new baseline par level for key ingredients set by the executive chef team, to stop out of stock items.
Region: managers can tailor the weekly cleaning checklist to their site layout (deadline extended to Friday) and report the changes at the next KPI meeting.
Region: B2B and PR spend should be tracked by opening a Kobas tab named B2B or PR rather than using discount buttons.
Covers rose by 658 (15.25%) week on week and spend per head fell by £1.97, on more £5 and free ramen redemptions; the report hopes this cools after the next two reward tiers stop being distributed.
Sales were up £284.02 (0.35%) week on week and £11,855.76 (17.56%) ahead of target.
Labour was 21.52% against the 21% target because more staff were needed each day for £5 ramen volume; the budget rota projects 21.30%.
Operational food cost was 32.49% against the 23% target after ordering more for the promotions.
Manchester had record student covers of about 4,900 and plans to adopt the edamame upselling approach from Shoreditch (AM Updates 21/10).
Manchester showed a strong Deliveroo uptick and is close to turning green (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: Michael made rider wait time the priority delivery metric this week, followed by ratings; sites need a 4.7 Deliveroo rating to compete and open times above 99.5% (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: GMs and head chefs must run a daily morning brief for FOH and BOH using the app's daily tab to review sales, delivery ratings and setups (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: failed delivery orders come from items marked out of stock on Kobas but not on Deliverect, so managers must update both, snooze unavailable extras by PLU and check Deliverect failed order statuses daily (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: stock edit permissions will be suspended for one week to see true variances, after wastage and comps were used to bring variances under 5% and distort Kobas ordering baselines (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: from next week automated Gemini meeting recordings and dashboard sign offs replace manual meeting notes and KPI sheets, with tasks synced to Asana and the legacy spreadsheets kept as a backup for now (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: third party discounted bookings are no longer allowed on Saturdays and are capped at a share of capacity on other days (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: Inka's sites generated around £6,000 of free ramen discounts, and FOH training days are scheduled across Nottingham, Leicester, Meadowhall and Manchester (AM Updates 21/10).
